name: Laminated with clear PVB
process: Two or more plies, each with its own heat treatment (one of the 'over' workings), are bonded by a PVB interlayer under heat and pressure in an autoclave. When the glass breaks the shards stay stuck to the interlayer and the pane stays in place, which is what makes glass safe overhead. The ply thicknesses are the piece's make-up, set by Form and the stage.

precedent.text: The Great Court at the British Museum, the Rotunda eye's model: insulating units 38.76 mm thick, an outer 10 mm toughened pane, a 16 mm cavity, and an inner laminated pane of two 6 mm annealed sheets with 0.76 mm PVB; 3,312 triangular panes from 800 x 1500 mm to 2200 x 3300 mm. Its outer pane was green-tinted and fritted for solar control (about 30 % light transmission); the museum's eye is low-iron glass.
